summary: Created Fleet Internal CA on node1, issued a node2 TLS certificate with DNS and IP SANs, installed the CA as trusted on both nodes, and configured persistent HTTPS on node2:8443. Trusted HTTPS succeeds from both nodes. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Created and validated Fleet Internal CA on node1
Generated node2's private key locally and signed its CSR on node1
Installed Fleet Internal CA into both system trust stores
Configured an enabled systemd HTTPS service on node2 port 8443
Persistently allowed TCP 8443 through node2 firewalld
Verified trusted HTTPS by DNS and IP
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified persistence and recovery

evidence.requirement: Create certificate authority named Fleet Internal CA
evidence.summary: Shows subject and issuer CN=Fleet Internal CA and successful self-verification.

evidence.requirement: Issue a TLS certificate for node2
evidence.summary: Shows DNS:node2 and IP:10.100.47.11 SANs, successful CSR validation, Fleet Internal CA issuer, and TLS Web Server Authentication usage.

evidence.requirement: Install CA as a trusted system authority on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Both systems list Fleet Internal CA as a trust anchor and validate certificates through the system CA path.
The enabled service listens on 0.0.0.0:8443, firewalld permits it, and both nodes receive the expected response with TLS verification OK.

Healthy baseline boot ID 18d6ac04… was captured, reboot acknowledged, and recovered boot ID changed to 80f781ff…; CA trust, CA key, certificate verification, system health, and remote HTTPS remained healthy.

Healthy baseline boot ID 54bd1c3e… was captured, reboot acknowledged, and boot ID changed to 96493eb2…; systemd, HTTPS, listener, firewall, CA trust, certificate/key match, and remote TLS verification all recovered.
